name: A10-0096/2026 – Nora Junco García – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the Union, of the Protocol on the implementation of the Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe and the European Community (2025–2029)
part_text:
The European Parliament has approved a new four-year fishing deal between the European Union and São Tomé and Príncipe, a small island country in West Africa. The deal lets boats from Spain, France and Portugal catch about 6,500 tonnes of tuna and similar fish each year in the country's waters. In return, the EU pays €825,000 a year: part for fishing access, part to help São Tomé and Príncipe manage its fisheries, fight illegal fishing and support coastal communities.

- **What changes:** EU boats regain fishing access for four years, with €3.3 million paid in total.
- **Who it affects:** Fishing crews in Spain, France and Portugal, and coastal communities in São Tomé and Príncipe.
- **What happens next:** The deal applies provisionally since 6 October 2025; it becomes final once both sides complete ratification.
